newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto up on options for chemical units.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto up on options for chemical units.

text.p: Shares of Monsanto Co rose 1-5/8 at 42-1/2 Thursday after the company said it is analyzing future alternatives for its chemical businesses.

"The market had been speculating about it for some time. The company is now saying yes, 'we're going to do something'," said Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenberg. "I expect the market to react positively."
Monsanto said it is considering several options, including separating the corporation into two public companies -- one a life sciences company and one a chemical firm.
Other options would be to merge the chemical businesses with one or more other companies, or to keep the businesses and restructuring them.
"I would say the chances of keeping it (chemicals) and restructuring it are pretty slim," said Wittenburg.

"I would think, ideally, they would like to sell it off or joint venture it," added Edward Jones anlayst Bill Fiala. He also noted that Monsanto had been expected to consider the future of its chemical operations for "quite some time.:
Fiala added that he believes the chemical businesses would be attractive to other companies.
Fiala also said the timing appears good for the likely separation of Monsanto's chemical businesses from its life sciences operations, which include agriculture, food additives and pharmaceuticals.

In a meeting with analysts earlier this month, Monsanto focused on its agricultural operations, analysts have said. Agricultural operations include genetically enhanced crops that are resistant to some herbicides or insect pests.
